newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian govt agency sees GDP up, unemployment down.
newsitem.headline: Belgian govt agency sees GDP up, unemployment down.

text.p: Belgium's Federal Planning Agency, preparing the ground for the government's 1998 budget, forecast on Tuesday a pick-up in economic growth and an increase in employment not seen since 1990.

In a statement, the agency said growth would accelerate in the second half of 1997 and in 1998. Exports and to a lesser extent corporate investment would boost the economy in 1997. In 1998 an additional impulse would come from private consumption.
Increasing employment would encourage Belgians to spend more.
It listed the following positive factors for growth:
- a growing international economy, particularly in neighbouring countries;
- a rise in the dollar, sterling and the lira, and the depreciation of the Belgian franc (estimated at over three percent in 1997);
- low international and Belgian interest rates;
